about: The king's men and the law at sea and in port (Plans/ai_fleets.md, phase 5). In 793 the law was kept at ports, tolls and borders: officials at the great toll places searched ships, above all those leaving the realm (Herstal 779: no byrnies out of the realm). Coastguard boats come only with Charles's coast defence of 800 and the fleets of 811 (Boulogne, Ghent). Which goods a law bites on, where and when: trade_rules.json 'laws'. Strictness is the chance a ship is searched at all; what's found depends on how much the hold hides. Starting guesses, uncertain items marked (?).

port_searches.about: chance a ship leaving is searched, by port; the rest of a zone takes its zone's default
port_searches.basis: the royal tolls of the Frankish realm (Dorestad, Quentovic - Gervold, procurator of the ports, 787-806), Kentish and London tolls in the 8th-century toll charters (?)

search.about_cover: a full hold hides up to 60% of what's searched for (cover = cover_max x how full the hold is)
search.about_gift: a gift of a tenth of the goods' worth (at least 12 d); taken more often by laxer officers (x (1 - strictness/2)); refused, they search hard and fine double

ai.about: the world's traders leaving a searching port, bound out of the realm, are searched by the same chances
